In the tradition of the multi-instrumentalists of the small jazz bands of the 1920s, Scott Robinson excels on multiple brass and reed horns. He has found a special niche in the jazz world today on the C melody, bass and baritone saxophones, as well as maintaining a reputation as a fine soloist and ensemble player on the more familiar brass and reed instruments. He shares his home with over two hundred horns and is always searching for rare additions for the collection. Scott has recorded with many jazz greats, including Frank Wess, Louie Bellson and Toshiko Akiyoshi. Recently he has recorded as a leader for Arbors Records where he chose to feature the rare and imposing contrabass saxophone on his release “Thinking Big.” A constant traveler, he has appeared at festivals in Europe, Japan and the Caribbean as well as jazz events at the Smithsonian and Carnegie Hall.
Scott was interviewed at the Allegheny Jazz Party in Chautauqua, New York on September 13, 1997 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
